To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription factor HIF-2a promotes colon cancer cell growth by potentiates YAP1 activity.
HIF-α increases YAP1 activity in CRC-derived cells and mouse models, and YAP activation is required for CRC cell growth under hypoxic conditions.
hypoxia-induced HIF-2alpha promotes colorectal cancer growth by potently up-regulating Yes-associated protein  1 (Yap1) activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HIF-α and YAP1 in CRC.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of cancer development and progression in the intestine.
the molecular mechanisms by which the HIF-2/YAP1 pathway contributes to the development of CRC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study demonstrates that HIF2α increases CRC growth by potentiation of Yap1 activity.
HIF-1/2α and YAP1 signaling pathways cooperate to promote cancer cell growth and that HIF-α and YAP signaling might be targeted in CRC patients.
HIF-1a and HIF-2a are both involved in colon cancer progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF-α is a master regulator of cell growth and proliferation.
HIF-α is a potent activator of YAP1 in the intestinal epithelium.
hypoxia and HIF-2 promote cancer cell proliferation by potentiating the Hippo signaling and YAP1 activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIF-α isoforms, in general, are not only transcriptional mediators but also potent activators of the YAP1 pathway in CRC.
HIF- 2α potentiates the activity of the Hippo pathway co-activator YAP1 in CRC, and this is a potential therapeutic target for CRC.
the HIF-2/YAP1 axis is a critical mediator of hypoxia-induced cell proliferation.
